name: Priya Evans

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, independent of employers, AI firms, unions, parties and government. Your answers are confidential. What happens on your normal factory shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I run a glass-bottle forming machine on a rotating shift. Hot glass drops into moulds, the machine shapes it, and I take samples to check the neck and wall before a crooked bottle reaches packing. I have a vocational certificate, but I learned the timing by listening to the machine for years. Nights leave me yawning over breakfast.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How does the shift fit with home and money?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Dan is a self-employed electrician. We have two school-age children, a mortgage and about eight months of expenses saved; my glassworks pay is good for an operator. Dan’s orders vary, so we budget from invoices actually paid. Other factories are nearby, but their shifts would have to fit pickup and the children’s evenings. I use AI occasionally for a school email, never to set the hot machine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the night crew that a little office automation is fine if somebody still checks the hot bottles. The furnace has its own clock; software cannot make us skip the sample tray.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The forming shift looks secure if AI stays modest. My wage is good, our eight-month reserve gives space, and there are other plants nearby. I would still watch Dan’s paid invoices rather than treat his next customer as money in the bank.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep running the forming machine and record the neck measurements on each sampled tray. After Dan’s crew and materials are paid, I would add a set amount from each newly cleared electrical invoice to our family savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the job. A quiet AI future would let us spend more thought on the shift rota than on headlines.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a bad sample tell you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A narrow neck means I check the mould timing before another rack fills. You can lose hundreds of bottles by pretending a camera will notice every fault. I like seeing the sample in my own hand.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use AI at the furnace if it was offered?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask another operator to test it first and show me the false alarms. At home I only use it for ordinary messages. A hot mould is no place for a guess from a chat window.

say: I would **tell** the crew routine office software does not replace hot-bottle sampling.
A **bad** neck still needs an operator to stop the forming machine promptly.
think: My **glassworks** wage and eight-month savings make a modest AI change manageable.
**Dan’s** future electrical bookings are uncertain until customers pay them.
do: **Keep** operating the forming machine and checking bottle-neck samples.
**Transfer** a set amount from each newly paid electrical invoice to family savings after costs.
feel: **Calm** about the shift, still attentive to the family rota.
S0.quote: A hot mould is no place for a guess from a chat window.
fieldNote: **Priya** measures hot-bottle samples herself and has only occasional AI use outside the factory.
Her **good** operator pay and eight months saved secure the plateau, while Dan’s self-employed receipts remain variable.
**New** savings come from cleared electrical work after its crew and materials are paid.

steps.text: Keep operating the forming machine and checking bottle-neck samples
Transfer fresh income from cleared electrical invoices into savings after costs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask management which order schedules are moving into software and when a robot swabber might reach the glass line. I would want the training place named before the job description changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The office can lose planning tasks first while I still swab moulds and check bottles. If one later operator oversees two forming machines, my hours could shrink even with eight months saved. Dan may get some installation work, but his customers have not promised enough to replace my wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would wait for a working swabber at the nearby glass plant, then ask for a paid supervised place on ours if management offers one with current hours and wage. I would take the training if the plant posts a real operator vacancy on the new line. If the place never appears, I would check local posted forming jobs whose pay and shift fit the mortgage and school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious about the possible cut to my hours. I can wait for proof because we have savings, but I cannot spend them forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why see the other plant first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Their first swabber might stop as often as our old mould oil pump did. I want to hear from an operator who has run it through a full night. A supplier's daytime robot demonstration tells me less than an operator's account of a full night.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a lower wage to keep a robot-line job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare it with the mortgage and Dan’s paid invoices, not a forecast of his next month. A lower wage might still work if the shift covers pickup, but I need the actual offer in writing. I would not resign for a rumour.

say: I would **ask** for separate dates for order software and robot swabbing.
A **paid** supervised place should lead to a real posted line vacancy.
think: The **first** software changes leave my hot-bottle work mostly intact.
A **later** two-machine roster could cut my own hours despite our reserve.
do: **Ask** for a paid supervised swabber place after another plant proves the equipment.
**Take** the place only with current hours, wage and a posted operator role.
**Check** local posted forming jobs if no place is offered, testing pay and pickup.
feel: **Anxious** about lost hours, with savings to check an actual offer first.
S1.quote: A supplier's daytime robot demonstration tells me less than an operator's account of a full night.
fieldNote: **Priya** waits for a full-night operating record, then conditions training on a paid supervised place and real posted role.
She does **not** presume Dan’s possible installation work will replace her higher factory wage.
The **no-course** fallback is a separate local vacancy search with mortgage and pickup tests.

steps.text: Take paid supervised swabber training only after proven operation and posted role at current terms
Check posted local forming jobs if no place is offered and pay and pickup fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew that AGI can take scheduling in 2028, while capable robots that swab and handle hot bottles follow around 2031. I would ask for the plant’s installation date, not a promise that everybody will be retained.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect most forming shifts to disappear when robots can run the hot end around 2031. Dan might wire some new cells before capable robots can do his work too, but that is temporary and unbooked. Eight months saved is useful, yet losing my wage and his orders would keep me awake at night.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month Dan and I would list the mortgage, school costs and only his confirmed invoices, then postpone the planned family trip. I would transfer part of my new shift wages into the reserve while I still earn them. If the glassworks cuts my hours, I would apply for posted local quality-inspection jobs only where paid safety instruction is offered and wages and shift cover our bills and pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about both household incomes. I would still take samples on tonight’s shift, but I would be awake afterwards doing the mortgage sums.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Dan take every robot-cell wiring request?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: He would price each request against the materials and the people he pays to help. I would not count a possible robot-cell job in our mortgage plan until a customer signs and pays. Work can sound busy and leave very little.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if there is no inspection job when your shifts fall?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the lender for hardship terms before we miss a payment, then search other posted factory roles that cover the mortgage and school travel. Eight months gives us time, not a reason to assume a vacancy. Dan and I would make that decision together.

say: I would **ask** for real dates before 2031 robots reach hot-glass work.
The 2028 **planning** change comes earlier than physical robot swabbing.
think: **Dan’s** electrical orders may also thin, and the eight-month reserve cannot replace two wages indefinitely.
do: **Postpone** the family trip and budget from confirmed electrical invoices.
**Transfer** part of newly earned glassworks shift wages to the reserve.
Apply for **inspection work** with paid safety training, bill-covering shifts and pickup; otherwise seek adequate factory work and lender terms before arrears.
feel: **Alarmed** by expected wage loss and awake doing mortgage sums.
S2.quote: I would not count a possible robot-cell job in our mortgage plan until a customer signs and pays.
fieldNote: **Priya** dates the main physical glassworks risk to around 2031, while 2028 AGI can change schedules.
Her **partner’s** possible robot-cell wiring is unbooked work, not an assumed replacement income.
She **cuts** a trip, adds fresh shift pay to reserves and requires a posted safe, bill-covering inspection role.

steps.text: Postpone the planned family trip and budget only confirmed electrical invoices
Transfer part of newly earned glassworks shifts into the reserve
Apply for inspection or factory vacancies fitting bills and pickup; require paid safety training for inspection
Ask lender about hardship before missed payment if no inspection vacancy appears

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the glass crew that five years can buy training if the plant starts early. AGI may handle schedules by 2031, and capable hot-end robots follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 51 when those robots arrive, I would rather have a new qualification than count on a night-shift operator post. Dan’s electrical business might need help testing new installations, but it cannot promise me wages from work not yet booked. I will not use our mortgage reserve to chase a title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the local college whether its electrical installation certificate is accepted for paid testing work, then enroll next year only if accepted, the tuition fits our budget and classes do not remove my glassworks pay or school pickup. I would keep my forming shifts during training. After I qualify, I would apply for a posted local testing role only if the wage and hours cover our mortgage; I would help Dan on signed jobs only when the work pays me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, though five years lets me test the course before leaving a shift. A qualification without a paid post would not carry our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually learn there?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Safe isolation and testing of an installed circuit, not a trick for writing invoices. Dan has shown me his paperwork, but he would not let me touch a live board without proper instruction. I agree with him.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the college course is not accepted for the role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the glassworks job and check posted machine-operator vacancies nearby, each on its own wage and shift terms. I would not buy the rejected course. There are other plants, though not every rota works for our children.

say: I would **ask** whether a recognised electrical certificate leads to paid testing work.
The **plant** should plan for 2034 hot-end robots before the glass crew loses shifts.
think: My **forming** role could shrink around age 51.
**Dan’s** business offers a possible bridge only when signed jobs actually pay me.
do: **Enrol** in accepted electrical testing training if safe instruction, tuition, paid shifts and school pickup fit.
**Keep** forming shifts during training and apply for posted bill-covering testing work after qualification.
**Check** local posted operator jobs if the certificate is rejected, testing wages and shift.
feel: **Anxious** about later work, with time to verify a course and vacancy.
S3.quote: A qualification without a paid post would not carry our mortgage.
fieldNote: **Priya** separates asking about a certificate from conditional actual enrollment and later application.
**Electrical** practice would require safe instruction, recognised credentials, affordable tuition and intact factory wages and pickup.
A **rejected** course leads to an independent local operator search, with no assumption of Dan’s unbooked pay.

steps.text: Enrol in accepted electrical course only with affordable tuition safe instruction protected wages and pickup
Apply for posted local testing work after qualification only if pay and hours cover mortgage
Check posted nearby operator work if course rejected and wages and shift fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell neighbours that ten years is enough to ask for honest plant dates and real apprenticeships. It is not enough to assume every child should become an electrician because one family business has orders now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 at the 2036 thinking-AI date and 56 when capable robots reach hot-end work around 2039. The children would be older and our mortgage might be smaller, but Dan’s electrical orders could also face competition. I would want another paid skill before relying on shares or savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the forming job while asking about a recognised electrical course, and enroll only if tuition fits, safe practical instruction is available and paid shifts and pickup are protected. After training I would apply for posted local testing work only if the wage covers our mortgage and the shift fits home. From each new paid glassworks overtime packet I would make an extra mortgage payment after the eight-month reserve stays intact.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy because the change is distant and my income is sound now. The long warning gives me room to check wages rather than guess.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you join Dan’s business full time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if signed electrical jobs after his costs leave a regular wage for me and cover our mortgage. I can help with invoices in the meantime. A family business cannot make an unpaid testing role safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to your children about study?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask what they enjoy, then show them the pay and training requirements for real local jobs. I would not push them into glass or wiring because I know those trades. Practical skills are useful, but they should have their own choice.

say: I would **ask** for honest robot dates and recognised training routes.
**Children** should see real job terms without being pushed into their parents’ trades.
think: My **factory** wage is sound now, but robot hot-end work could arrive around 2039.
**Dan’s** paid orders may change too, so savings cannot be the whole wage plan.
do: **Keep** the forming role while checking an accepted safe electrical course.
**Enrol** only if tuition, paid shifts and pickup fit; apply later to bill-covering posted testing work.
**Pay** extra mortgage principal from newly paid overtime after keeping the cash reserve.
feel: **Uneasy** about distant change while current wages remain secure.
S4.quote: A family business cannot make an unpaid testing role safe.
fieldNote: **Priya** keeps the current high wage while examining a recognised, safe electrical qualification.
She **conditions** future testing applications on posted local wages and workable shifts rather than her partner’s hopeful bookings.
**Extra** mortgage payment comes from fresh overtime after the existing reserve is protected.

steps.text: Keep operating the forming machine while checking electrical course terms
Enrol in recognised safe electrical training only if tuition wages and pickup fit
Apply for posted local testing work after qualification only if wages and shift cover mortgage
Pay extra mortgage principal from new overtime after cash reserve remains intact

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The two-year AGI picture worries me most because hot-end robots could take most forming shifts around 2031 while Dan’s electrical orders may also change. Recognised training that preserves my wage and posted local work with safe instruction would help us protect the mortgage.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I did not ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who keeps the glass furnace running safely during a changeover. A furnace cannot be switched off like an office light. The night crew will know first if a promised robot plan has holes.

headlineQuote: A furnace cannot be switched off like an office light.
portrait: **Priya** Evans, 43, runs a hot-glass forming machine and holds a vocational certificate.
She and her **self-employed** electrician partner Dan have two school-age children, a mortgage and about eight months of expenses saved.
Her **own** operator pay is high; she budgets Dan’s variable work from cleared invoices, not possible future jobs.
She **uses** AI occasionally outside work and waits for proven equipment, safe paid training and real posted roles.
**Fast** AGI alarms her because scheduling changes by 2028 but capable hot-end robots threaten forming shifts around 2031.
biggestWorry: **Fast** AGI could remove most of her forming hours around 2031 while Dan’s electrical orders also weaken.
whatWouldHelp: **Recognised** training with protected wages, safe instruction and posted local work with mortgage-covering pay would help.
